newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kemira says pigments weak, profit steady.
newsitem.headline: Kemira says pigments weak, profit steady.

text.p: Finnish chemicals group Kemira Oy said in a statement on Tuesday the consolidated full-year operating profit would be roughly on par with last year's despite a weak performance for its pigments unit.
"Management expects that operating income for the full year 1996 will be roughly at the same level as in 1995," Kemira said. In 1995, group operating profit was 1.34 billion markka.
Weak titanium dioxide markets had hit Kemira Pigments.
"(Its) results for ... the year as a whole are expected to be significantly lower than in 1995, close to breakeven on the operating income level," it said.
In 1995, the pigments unit's operating profit was 255 million markka -- almost one fifth of consolidated operating profit and 12 percent of the unit's net sales.
In January-April, Kemira had said pigments posted operating profit corresponding to 3.5 percent of group operating profit for the period, and to 3.3 percent of the unit's sales.

"As a result of weak sales volumes and an erosion of prices that has amounted to 10 percent since the beginning of the year, and mainly in the second tertial, this business will not meet earlier expectations," Kemira said.
But it repeated that group net profit would go on improving.
"Kemira expects that it will be able to report continued growth in net income before taxes for the 1996 financial year," it said.
"This is primarily due to the continued good performance of the three other core businesses and the reduction in financial expenses," it added.
Last year, group pre-tax profit rose to 721 million markka from 327 million. Net financial expenses were 619 million markka, up from 587 million.
"A considerable reduction in net financial charges enables management to continue to expect to achieve growth in 1996 net earnings before taxes," Kemira said.
Its Agro fertilisers unit continued to benefit from positive market fundamentals and "the outlook for prices and volumes remains good," it said.
Kemira Chemicals was performing in line with expectations. "Operating income for the first eight months and for the year as a whole will show growth," Kemira said.
It said paint maker Tikkurila was also expected to show operating profit growth for the eight-month and the full-year periods.
